name: INNOVIVA

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: My refusal leans on the cliff, and the cliff argument is weaker than it looks. Generic Advair has existed since 2016 and RELVAR/BREO royalties are still 'stable' a decade later, because the ELLIPTA device and formulation are hard to copy - inhaled generics routinely fail to arrive on schedule. If the royalty runs materially past 2031, then a market requiring a 23-38% ANNUAL decline in FCFF is far too pessimistic and the name is straightforwardly cheap: the enterprise value corrected for the investment portfolio is roughly $511M against $187.5M of normalised FCFF, which is 2.7x.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Two things. Any ANDA filing or Paragraph IV notice against FF/VI or UMEC/VI, and GSK's own disclosure of Ellipta franchise erosion - GSK reports Trelegy/Breo/Anoro sales quarterly, and a step-down in Innoviva's royalty line would appear within a quarter of it. And the trajectory of IST: whether $150M of 2026 US sales becomes $300M+ by 2029, which is what replacing the royalty requires.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Not yet, and that is the honest state of it. The royalty is stable TODAY at $59.8M a quarter and +2% sequentially, which supports the counter. I found no ANDA or Paragraph IV disclosure against FF/VI in the 10-K or 10-Q, and the 10-K discusses generic competition only as a risk factor. Against the counter, the 10-K says in terms that royalties from RELVAR/BREO and ANORO 'are expected to represent the majority of our foreseeable future revenues from GSK', so the concentration is not disputed.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The date. I could not find the end of the LABA Collaboration Agreement royalty term in either the 10-K or the 10-Q - the agreement runs to the last-to-expire patent rather than to a stated date, and the filings do not tabulate those patents for the GSK-partnered products the way they do for the owned products. The 2030-10-11 expiry plus pediatric exclusivity to 2031 is from a secondary patent database, not from a filing, and I am recording it as such. Also unresolved: HealthCare Royalty is entitled to quarterly royalties on worldwide GIAPREZA net sales until 2031 or a cap, which is a real claim on the IST cash flows that appears in neither total_debt nor the enterprise value, and I could not size its remaining balance.

what_changed: Q2 2026 (reported 2026-08-05): revenue $119.6M against $100.3M, income from operations $50.9M against $48.8M, but a net LOSS of $83.4M ($1.14 basic) driven by $161.0M of unfavourable fair-value change on equity and long-term investments, principally Armata's share price. Gross GSK royalty revenue $59.8M, described by the company as 'remains stable', +2% sequentially. Innoviva Specialty Therapeutics net product sales $51.8M, +46% year over year ($36.6M US, $15.2M ex-US: GIAPREZA $21.0M, XACDURO $12.0M, XERAVA $3.3M), with the company on track for at least $150M of US net product sales in 2026. Royalty and product receivables $110.6M, +25% y/y. Nortiva Bio launched 2026-06-18 as a clinical-stage subsidiary. XACDURO, ZEVTERA and NUZOLVENCE were named 2026 Prix Galien USA finalists.
consensus_case: At $20.66 Innoviva holds $570.4M of cash and $669.5M of strategic healthcare investments - $1,240M, or $17.16 per share of a $20.66 price - so the market is paying roughly $3.50 a share, about $253M of equity value, for the operating business. It does that because the operating business is mostly a royalty that dies. Gross GSK royalty revenue is $59.8M a quarter, ~$239M a year, and the principal patent covering RELVAR/BREO ELLIPTA expires 2030-10-11 with pediatric exclusivity to 2031 - four to five years out, i.e. INSIDE the explicit DCF window. The market is also discounting the investment portfolio heavily, and rightly: $457.7M of the $669.5M is Armata Pharmaceuticals, a clinical-stage bacteriophage company whose mark just cost Innoviva $161.0M in one quarter and which Innoviva keeps funding through successive term loans. That is not cash, it is a commitment.
base_case_rationale: No single five-year FCFF growth rate describes this company, and supplying one would launder a structural error into a fair value. Innoviva is three things a single two-stage FCFF model cannot add up: a royalty stream with a contractual and dated end, a specialty pharma growing net product sales 46% with patents running to 2033-2045, and a $669.5M portfolio of marked investments dominated by one illiquid controlled biotech. The engine's terminal value capitalises whatever the fifth year produces at 2% growth IN PERPETUITY, and roughly 58% of today's revenue contractually stops around 2030-31. That is not a growth-rate problem, it is the wrong model form, and the schema has no field to override terminal growth.
key_risks: ~58% of revenue is a GSK royalty on two inhaled products whose principal patent protection lapses around 2030-31, inside the valuation window
$457.7M of the $669.5M investment portfolio is Armata, an illiquid controlled clinical-stage position that cost $161.0M of marks in one quarter and which Innoviva keeps lending to
The HealthCare Royalty obligation on GIAPREZA sales to 2031 is a claim on IST cash flow that sits in neither debt nor EV
Net income is dominated by marks, so reported earnings say almost nothing about the operating business in any given quarter
watch_for: Any Paragraph IV / ANDA notice on fluticasone furoate-vilanterol or umeclidinium-vilanterol
GSK's quarterly Ellipta franchise disclosure and any step-down in Innoviva's royalty line from the $59.8M quarterly run rate
IST US net product sales against the $150M 2026 commitment, and whether the 46% growth rate holds into 2027
Further Armata funding rounds or term loans - each one converts a marked asset into a cash commitment
